summary:
Relic Star is a story-driven space archaeology game that explores the forgotten legacy of NASA's abandoned scientific equipment on the Moon and Mars. Players take on the role of a space explorer, scanning planetary surfaces, discovering historical hardware, investigating its components, and documenting the scientific contributions of each relic.

Inspired by the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten," the game transforms historical NASA mission information into an interactive exploration experience. It combines verified NASA resources NSSDCA, NASA Space archives and PDS with immersive storytelling and simulated gameplay to help players understand why these machines were deployed, what they accomplished, and why their transmissions eventually ceased.

By connecting space exploration, science, and digital storytelling, Relic Star aims to preserve the legacy of these silent machines and inspire curiosity about planetary exploration and the history of space missions.
details:
Relic Star – Project Details

The Problem and Our Solution

Space exploration has left behind scientific equipment on the Moon and Mars. Although some of these machines have stopped transmitting or are no longer operational, their scientific contributions remain valuable.

Relic Star addresses the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten" by turning the history of these machines into an interactive space archaeology experience. Instead of simply reading about historical equipment, players explore planetary environments, discover relics, investigate hardware, and preserve their findings in a digital archive.

How the Game Works

Players begin their journey on the Moon, with Mars planned as a future expedition. Using an exploration interface, they can:

  • Explore a planetary environment using keyboard and mouse controls.
  • Scan the surroundings to detect historical NASA equipment.
  • Investigate discovered hardware and examine its components.
  • Review verified historical information and available mission records.
  • Document discoveries and transmit findings to the archive.
  • Revisit previously discovered equipment through the archive.

The game connects scanning, investigation, documentation, and archiving into one exploration loop.

NASA Data and Scientific Authenticity

Relic Star uses NASA historical mission documents and planetary research resources to ground its discoveries in real space exploration history.

We distinguish between three types of information:

  1. Verified NASA Facts – Information supported by NASA documents and other cited scientific resources.
  2. Simulated Gameplay – Interactive mechanics and environmental representations created for the game.
  3. Simulated Transmission – Fictional in-game communication used for storytelling, not presented as an actual NASA transmission.

When information is unavailable or cannot be verified, it is identified as UNKNOWN rather than presented as fact. Our 3D hardware models are game representations, not official NASA engineering models.

Technology and Development

The project was developed using:

  • React and TypeScript
  • Three.js / React Three Fiber
  • Vite
  • HTML and CSS
  • NASA historical and planetary resources
  • AI-assisted development tools

The game uses a modular architecture for planetary environments, player controls, hardware discovery, investigation, and persistent save data.

Impact and Future Vision

Relic Star aims to make space history more engaging and accessible, especially for students, educators, and people interested in astronomy and planetary science.

Our goal is to demonstrate that a machine does not lose its scientific value simply because it stops working. Its discoveries, mission history, and contribution to science remain part of humanity's exploration legacy.

Future development may expand planetary exploration, improve scientific archives, and introduce additional historical hardware discoveries.
